translationRepairs: In 1862 Li Hongzhang led eight thousand Huai Army men to Shanghai, and Songlin went with him. West of the city he fought the rebel kings Li Xiucheng and Tan Shaoguang and routed a rebel host of one hundred thousand.

In 1862 Li Hongzhang led eight thousand Huai Army men to Shanghai, and Songlin went with him. West of the city he fought the rebel Loyal King Li Xiucheng and the rebel Prince Mu Tan Shaoguang and routed a rebel host of one hundred thousand.
The source supplies distinct Taiping titles for both men; retaining Loyal King and Prince Mu is more informative than collapsing them to generic rebel kings.
In 1861 Anqing fell; he was promoted to battalion commander and given the title Brave Baturu.
In 1861 Anqing fell; he was promoted to colonel and given the title Brave Baturu.
Youji is rendered as colonel throughout this volume's established Qing rank ladder; major would introduce a new and lower equivalent.

In 1856 he joined Zeng Guoquan's forces, marched to relieve Jiangxi, took Anfu, and helped clear Yongxin, Taihe, Wan'an, Lianhua subprefecture, and Longquan, for which he was commended and given the rank of corporal.

In 1856 he joined Zeng Guoquan's forces, marched to relieve Jiangxi, took Anfu, and helped clear Yongxin, Taihe, Wan'an, Lianhua subprefecture, and Longquan, for which he was commended and given the rank of platoon officer.
Bazong is rendered as platoon officer in the surrounding Draft History of Qing chapters; 'corporal' is too low and 'file leader (batotal)' is needlessly obscure.
He took Zhelin, Fengxian, Nanhui, Chuansha, and Jinshan, raised the siege of Songjiang, recovered Qingpu, and was promoted to sergeant.
He took Zhelin, Fengxian, Nanhui, Chuansha, and Jinshan, raised the siege of Songjiang, recovered Qingpu, and was promoted to company commander.
Qianzong is consistently rendered as company commander in the surrounding chapters; sergeant is too low.
He pressed the campaign against Changzhou, relieved Major General Tang Diankui at Benniu, and broke the siege there.
He pressed the campaign against Changzhou, relieved brigade general Tang Diankui at Benniu, and broke the siege there.
Zongbing is rendered as brigade general in adjacent Draft History of Qing chapters; major general is inconsistent with that rank ladder.
In 1852 he enlisted, first under Li Mengqun, judicial commissioner of Hubei. When Hanyang fell he was promoted to corporal.
In 1852 he enlisted, first under Li Mengqun, judicial commissioner of Hubei. When Hanyang fell he was promoted to platoon officer.
The established corpus equivalent for bazong is platoon officer, not corporal or the opaque loanword batotal.
In 1858 he fought at Hukou and was promoted to sergeant.
In 1858 he fought at Hukou and was promoted to company commander.
Qianzong is the company-commander rank in this translation's established ladder.
He took the rebel stronghold at Chigang Ridge outside Anqing and was made battalion commander.
He took the rebel stronghold at Chigang Ridge outside Anqing and was made colonel.
Youji is rendered as colonel in the established Qing rank ladder.
He also helped take the Sanhe garrison outside Hefei and raise the siege of Lu'an, and was commended as sergeant.
He also helped take the Sanhe garrison outside Hefei and raise the siege of Lu'an, and was commended as company commander.
Qianzong is consistently a company commander here; sergeant understates the office.
In 1863 he captured the Yangshe garrison at Jiangyin, was made battalion commander, and received the title Striking Brave Baturu.
In 1863 he captured the Yangshe garrison at Jiangyin, was made colonel, and received the title Striking Brave Baturu.
Youji is rendered as colonel in the established Qing rank ladder.
Major General Ju Yaoqian brought his gunboats to Xujing, and Sergeant Yuan Guangzheng entered the city to help hold it.
Brigade general Ju Yaoqian brought his gunboats to Xujing, and company commander Yuan Guangzheng entered the city to help hold it.
The sentence contains both zongbing and qianzong; the revision aligns both with the corpus's brigade-general and company-commander equivalents.
